title: Reactions & Listening
description: The little words that show you're listening: surprise, sympathy, relief and 'and then?'. Several are friendly and casual, and the notes say which to use with older people.

phrases.registerNotes: The all-purpose 'I see' while someone explains something, polite with anyone. Among friends it shrinks to Oh, gitu.
Said softly while someone is talking, to show you're following. Said fast and loud, it sounds impatient, like 'yeah, yeah, I know'.
phrases.pitfallNote: It means 'I hear you', not 'I agree'. Indonesians use it the same way, so a string of iya from them isn't a promise either.

phrases.registerNotes: Mild interest or surprise, polite with anyone, with the voice rising at the end.
phrases.pitfallNote: Said flat, Oh, ya. means 'oh, right' as something comes back to you: Oh, ya, saya lupa (Oh, right, I forgot).

phrases.registerNotes: Half-playful disbelief; Masa, sih? is the casual version. It can sound as if you doubt them, so with an older person Oh, ya? is safer.
Between friends, and Beneran? means the same. To someone older, Sungguh? or Oh, ya? sounds more respectful.
Wah opens most happy surprise: Wah, bagus. Wah, enak. Hebat praises what someone has done, like passing an exam or finishing a race.
For pain, and for small troubles: Aduh, saya lupa (Oh no, I forgot). Waduh is a stronger, slightly comic version.
Shock, dismay or exasperation at what you've just heard: Ya ampun, mahal sekali. Astaga is another common one.
phrases.cultureNote: Many Muslims say Ya Allah in the same moment; as a non-Muslim, Ya ampun is the natural choice.

phrases.registerNotes: Sympathy for someone else's bad luck: Kasihan, dia sakit lagi. Kasihan sekali for real misfortune.
phrases.pitfallNote: Spelled kasihan, but usually said kasian.

phrases.registerNotes: Relief at good news: someone is feeling better, the flight landed safely. It comes from syukur, gratitude to God.
phrases.cultureNote: You'll often hear Alhamdulillah (praise be to God) in the same place; Syukurlah suits anyone.

phrases.registerNotes: Disappointment, mild or real: Sayang sekali, tokonya sudah tutup. Friends say Sayang banget.
phrases.pitfallNote: Sayang is also 'darling' and 'to love'. At the start of a reaction like this it only means 'what a pity'.

phrases.registerNotes: With a rising voice, to keep a story going. Terus is the everyday spoken word; Lalu? is more careful, if you're listening to someone much older.
When something suddenly makes sense: Dia kerja sampai malam? Pantas saja capek. Among friends it's Pantesan.
